title: LayerSkip: Enabling Early Exit Inference and Self-Speculative Decoding
technique: layer dropout + early-exit loss training recipe; self-speculative decoding that drafts with early layers and verifies with remaining layers sharing KV cache

optimized_metrics.evidence: We present LayerSkip, an end-to-end solution to speed-up inference of large language models (LLMs).
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: speedup is calculated as the acceleration of average inference time per token compared to the "Autoregressive" baseline on the same setting

optimized_metrics.evidence: The advantage of speculative decoding is that it leads to faster inference compared to the main model, but requires a larger memory footprint and complexity in implementation to maintain key-value (KV) cache in two different models. ... this paper also proposes combining exiting early with speculative decoding to propose a self-speculative decoding approach that does not require an additional model or auxiliary layers.
self-speculative decoding ... has no drop in accuracy; training recipe increases the accuracy of early exit at earlier layers; last-layer accuracy should be maintained

headline_claim.text: We implement our inference solution and show speedups of up to 2.16x on summarization for CNN/DM documents, 1.82x on coding, and 2.0x on TOPv2 semantic parsing task.

reported_metrics.where: Tables: 'Acc. per Sec.' tokens/s per sample (single stream)
ROUGE-2, EM, perplexity, early-exit accuracy per layer (Fig 8-11)

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Following Zhang et al. (2023), speedup is calculated as the acceleration of average inference time per token compared to the "Autoregressive" baseline on the same setting.
metric_definitions.notes: single-sequence per-token time ratio vs HuggingFace autoregressive baseline

metric_definitions.definition_quote: throughput measured as tokens per second averaged over the sampled dataset
metric_definitions.notes: per-sample generation rate, not system throughput

metric_definitions.definition_quote: token acceptance rate for the self speculation algorithm (how often verification accepts each of the draft tokens)

load_regime: per-sample generation, greedy, max 512 new tokens; batch size not stated (single-sequence latency setting implied); no serving load
tradeoff_acknowledged: Early exit trades accuracy for latency; training recipe can slightly drop last-layer accuracy (e.g. 3% on TOPv2 without escale tuning; larger drop for Llama3 continual pretraining).
hardware: NVIDIA H100 (continual pretraining, TOPv2), A100 (code finetuning)
workloads: CNN/DM, XSUM, HumanEval, MBPP, TOPv2, NaturalQuestions etc.
extractor_notes: Primary metric is wall-clock speedup of single-stream decoding; batch size not specified in what I read (grep found no inference batch size). Includes training-side contributions (layer dropout).
